title: Why Does the Sun Make You SNEEZE? 🤧
description:
You step out of a dark cinema into bright sunshine and... ACHOO. That's the photic sneeze reflex, and roughly one in four people have it. It isn't a cold: it's the sudden jump from dark to bright light that sets it off. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Why? Nobody has proved it yet. The leading idea is crossed wires: the nerve from your eyes runs close to the trigeminal nerve, which feels irritation in your nose, and a sudden flood of light may spill from one into the other, so your brain thinks something is up your nose. It runs in families, and in 1978 four doctors (sun sneezers themselves) gave it a real medical name: ACHOO syndrome, for Autosomal dominant Compelling Helio-Ophthalmic Outburst. Sunglasses help. Aristotle was already asking about it 2,300 years ago.
